results.summary: This project implements a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor for RISC-V instructions. It reads instruction addresses and ground truth branch directions via SPI, predicting branch outcomes. Due to memory constraints, prediction is not single-cycle. The design can be tested using a provided C++ functional simulator and CocoTB tests, requiring external hardware to drive inputs and read outputs. It is notable for its implementation of a perceptron-based predictor and its detailed simulation infrastructure.

This project is a simplified Karplus-Strong string synthesis audio synthesizer. It uses a SPI interface for control and configuration, and outputs synthesized sound samples via an I2S transmitter interface. Testing requires an I2S DAC to receive the audio samples. The design is based on established papers on digital sound synthesis.

This project displays the letter 'H' on an LED display. It is implemented using Wokwi and appears to be a simple demonstration or template project. The description for testing is minimal, suggesting specific switches need to be turned on. No external hardware is explicitly mentioned beyond the implied LED display.

This design implements a slow, 3-bit unsigned multiplier that prioritizes area efficiency over speed. It streams input values over multiple clock cycles and then streams the 6-bit product back. The result is available after 18 cycles. Testing can be done via a web interface or by connecting Pmods. The design is intended for educational purposes and demonstrates a trade-off between resources and performance.

This project is a UART transceiver designed to handle 8-bit data frames with little-endian transmit and receive signals. The description of how it works and how to test it is currently incomplete. No external hardware requirements are specified. Further documentation is needed to fully understand its capabilities and usage.

This project replicates the 74181 4-bit slice arithmetic logic unit (ALU) and instantiates two of them to create an 8-bit ALU. It includes a SPI slave peripheral for loading and reading data, supporting all four SPI modes. A multiplexer taps user logic for debugging on a 7-segment display. Testing involves using an SPI master, like the RP2040's SPI1 peripheral. Silicon tests confirm the SPI interface works correctly.

This project simulates an elevator interface on a digital clock display, controlled by board switches. The display shows floor numbers and indicates the elevator's state (moving up, down, or idle). The project uses 7-segment display outputs for visualization. Testing involves using the provided switches to select floors. A LED display is required as external hardware to visualize the operation.

This project is a PWM module controllable via an SPI interface, designed to output analog results using digital signals by varying the duty cycle. It allows adjustment of output pulse width to regulate average voltage. Testing involves programming registers over SPI and using override pins for direct PWM testing. An SPI master device and a tool to view the PWM signal are required as external hardware.

This project is an 8-bit Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) classifier that compares an input data vector against two class prototypes. It calculates the Hamming distance to each prototype and outputs the winning class and the distances. Testing involves resetting the design, applying input data, configuring mode and class selection, and asserting start. No external hardware is required for this design. The design is notable for its application of HDC principles.

This design is a multi-mode digital signal processing unit that supports filtering, multiply-accumulate, edge detection, and nonlinear compression. It takes two 8-bit inputs and uses a 2-bit mode selection to determine its operation, also utilizing a stored previous output value. Testing is performed via simulation using a provided testbench, which generates a waveform file for analysis. No external hardware is required for simulation.
